Team / Peter — after running the numbers and simulating the token flows, here’s a pragmatic sizing and ops plan tailored to Argus’ profile. I’m attaching a short model and the capacity spreadsheet.

Executive summary:
- Baseline sizing: 1 x H100-equivalent slab (reserved pool) sized to comfortably handle sustained morning peaks at ~100 tokens/sec with a 1.5x buffer. That maps to ~0.5–0.6 H100 slab-equivalents for steady-state but we reserve 1 slab to simplify commit and meet p95 targets.
- Burst buffer: two hot burst lanes (pre-warmed) that add capacity to handle microbursts up to 600 tokens/sec without p95 degradation. Each lane is a narrow-slab instance with quick attach (~30s) and pre-warmed KV caches for the common prompt patterns.
- Fractioning logic: route requests by token-size and latency necessity — small single-turn requests go to dedicated hot lanes, large multi-turn extractions can be routed to the reserved slab when latency budget allows. This reduces cache-thrashing.
- Latency assumptions used in the model: 300ms p95 requires warm KV cache hit rates >= 85%, model quantized (4-bit) with optimized kernels, and request batching capped to preserve latency (batch window <= 20ms).

Numbers (model-based):
- Morning sustained demand: 100 tokens/sec -> reserved slab gives headroom 1.5x -> effective capacity 150 tokens/sec.
- Microburst absorption: burst lanes add +450 tokens/sec combined (2 lanes @ ~225 tokens/sec each pre-warmed) yielding peak absorption up to ~600 tokens/sec for short windows.
- Recommended commit: 1 reserved slab + 2 hot burst lanes. Optional add-on: standby cold burst (on-demand) for rare >5x events.

Ops notes and caveats:
- Warm-up: pre-warming KV cache for common prefixes reduces tail significantly. We recommend a scheduled pre-warm run 10–15 minutes before the morning window.
- Cold-start: full cold starts (no cache) will exceed p95; include fallbacks to a smaller, lower-latency distilled model for aggressive cold situations.
- Monitoring & auto-fallbacks: set an automatic threshold at sustained >500 tokens/sec for >2min to shift lower-priority workloads off reserved slab and prioritize critical extractions.

Attachments included:
- argus_capacity_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 58KB) — per-slab token/sec mapping, GPU SKU equivalencies, and cost delta for 12/6/3-month commits.
- tps_latency_model.pdf (pdf, 45KB) — simulation graphs (p50/p95/p99 under various cache-hit and batch sizes).

- Peter: confirm whether Argus wants the 1-slab commit with monthly burst billing or a larger 3-month commit for a lower unit cost.
